tasks.short: Record pesticide use, crop yields and costs

steps.what: Obtain actual crop activity, pesticide use, yield and cost details with their sources
Record crop information, pesticide use, yields and costs on the required record
Compile recorded crop yields and costs by plot and reporting period
Check crop records and summaries for missing details, units and source mismatches

tasks.design: Capture crop event details once in the field-record category of {OPS_SYSTEM}, then use native summaries for plot yields and costs. Keep actual-use capture and source checks with the worker; product warnings assist record checking and do not authorise pesticide application.
tasks.previous_blocker: Field details are copied from notes into separate records and summaries, with mixed units and missing plot links.
tasks.enabler_now: Native field forms and plot summaries can reuse explicitly captured events without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing actual treated area, actual product use and which costs belong to the crop.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish what happened in the field from a planned instruction or estimated quantity.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate record entry and arithmetic; responsibility for actual-use accuracy remains human.

reach.task: Resolve an unmatched cost or yield allocation to a plot
reach.learn: Plot identifiers, units and cost-source traceability

evidence.claim: AgroVision Crops logs sowing, spraying, fertilising and harvest on a phone and warns about unauthorised products or exceeded authorised dose.
LetsGrow provides greenhouse crop registration directly at the growing location.
Plot summaries can aggregate captured quantities and allocated costs deterministically; the saving estimate here is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is farmworker record preparation and checking, not selecting, applying or authorising crop-protection treatment, growing crops, harvesting or financial bookkeeping.

Worker produces event date and time, plot id, crop, activity, product identifier, actual quantity, unit and treated area in s1; for harvest, lot id and actual yield with unit; for cost, source document id, amount, currency and plot allocation. Its full 45 hours cover collection, verification and phone capture; planned advice never proves actual use.

Farm manager already maintains plot id, crop and area in the plot register outside this task. Bookkeeper produces existing posted cost documents, and a weighbridge operator or worker produces existing harvest results during unchanged operations outside recording. Missing sources are investigated during s1 or retained review; no new source capture is silently transferred.

s2 retains 10 hours for missing-field entry, unit checks and manual fallback. s3 aggregates only matched plot ids and compatible units, excludes unknown allocations and exposes incomplete totals rather than inventing values.

Test native field forms and summaries before integration. No machine terminal feed is assumed; extra capture cannot be treated as free. Product-database updates, mappings and exception checks are costed below.
Existing processing runtime earns no labour saving. No worker productivity ranking is introduced; employee-linked recording requires appropriate local consultation and permissions.
unknowns: Quality of plot and cost identifiers
Existing phone access in the field
research_questions: Can each summary total be traced to captured actual quantities and a matching plot without extra duplicate entry?

already_counted.description: Collect and capture actual events, complete records and check sources

incremental.description: Maintain units, plot mappings and product-database updates and inspect failed summaries

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+10+0+15=70; gross 30 less upkeep 2 gives net 28. E1 scenario removes duplicate entry and manual plot arithmetic only after fully counted capture. Missing source records, poor connectivity or existing native summaries can leave no gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct and monitor seasonal planting and harvesting help

steps.what: Direct casual and seasonal help during planting and harvesting with clear practical instructions
Monitor seasonal workers' field work, demonstrate corrections and respond to changing conditions

tasks.design: Retain field direction, observation and coaching with the worker. Existing instructions in {DOCS} may support the briefing, but no automated worker monitoring or allocation is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safe and effective field work depends on practical explanation and changing crop conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: No new technology is needed for this unchanged supervision.
tasks.still_hard: Language differences, uneven experience and conditions that change during the day.
tasks.human_edge: Demonstrate work, notice misunderstanding and intervene promptly.
tasks.altitude: Field supervision time and authority stay unchanged.

reach.task: Adjust a field assignment when crop or worker conditions change
reach.learn: Task limits, safe demonstrations and clear escalation

evidence.claim: Field direction and responsive supervision require live observation and communication rather than an automated productivity record.

assumptions: Boundary covers only the focal worker's briefing and supervision, not seasonal workers' own planting or harvest labour.
Farm manager provides existing priorities; focal worker observes conditions and explains assignments within the retained steps. No structured worker score or machine action is proposed.
Native document access stays unchanged. Zero incremental upkeep because no new recording, allocation or monitoring system is introduced.
research_questions: Which mistakes are prevented by practical demonstration rather than written instructions alone?

already_counted.description: Direct seasonal help and supervise field work

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and net zero. Retain all instruction, observation and intervention; no work is transferred to seasonal staff to create a saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect, grade, sort, store and treat harvested crops

steps.what: Inspect harvested crops and grade their condition against the required standard
Sort harvested crops into the appropriate grade and handling groups
Place crops in suitable storage and participate in authorised post-harvest treatment

tasks.design: Retain physical crop inspection, sorting, storage and authorised treatment with the worker. Existing instructions in {DOCS} remain the source; no vision line, robot or treatment controller is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: Variable crop condition and physical handling dominate this task.
tasks.enabler_now: No new software can replace the stated physical work without a separate equipment and process change.
tasks.still_hard: Subtle deterioration, mixed quality and crop-specific storage requirements.
tasks.human_edge: Notice fragile or deteriorating crops and handle them appropriately.
tasks.altitude: Hands-on time and treatment authority stay unchanged.

reach.task: Resolve an uncertain crop quality grade

evidence.claim: Physical crop grading and post-harvest handling remain manual without specialised inspection and handling equipment.

assumptions: Boundary is worker participation under existing grading, storage and permitted treatment instructions, not selecting chemicals or authorising new treatments.
Farm supervisor provides existing standards and instructions; worker produces observed grades in s1 with all time retained. No structured grade drives a machine or removes capture time.
All sorting and storage remain physical. Check existing native instruction access before considering software; no build is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because there is no new equipment, treatment logic or digital record process.
research_questions: Which quality differences require handling or opening the crop to inspect?

already_counted.description: Inspect and grade crops, sort physically and complete authorised handling

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and net zero. Retain every physical and judgement step; a record app is not counted as sorting or storing crops.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inform farm managers of crop progress

steps.what: Observe crop progress and identify changes or concerns worth raising
Inform farmers or farm managers of crop progress and discuss uncertainties

tasks.design: Retain direct observation and the crop-progress discussion. Existing field records in {OPS_SYSTEM} can be consulted, but they do not replace current observations or explanation of uncertainty.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recorded activities do not necessarily show the current crop condition.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records support the discussion without requiring a new reporting service.
tasks.still_hard: Separating a temporary change from a meaningful crop concern.
tasks.human_edge: Explain what was observed and what remains uncertain.
tasks.altitude: Observation and reporting conversation time remain unchanged; crop decisions stay with the manager.

reach.task: Turn an observed crop concern into a question for the farm manager
reach.learn: Clear observation descriptions and limits of inference

evidence.claim: An activity log alone does not establish current crop progress; this design retains observation and human explanation.

assumptions: Boundary covers worker observation and informing the manager, not the manager's decision or agronomic diagnosis.
Worker produces current observations in s1 with all 45 hours retained. No structured progress status, image model or sensor feed is assumed.
Native record access is unchanged and earns no saving. Zero incremental upkeep because no new reporting, data capture or automated summary is introduced.
Observations overlapping routine field inspection must be allocated once in a role roll-up.
unknowns: How crop progress is currently communicated
research_questions: What useful crop context is communicated orally that is absent from activity records?

already_counted.description: Observe crop progress and discuss it with the manager

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and net zero. Retain observation and communication; no unobserved report-writing baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The worker can avoid duplicate crop records and manual summaries while retaining supervision, crop handling and progress discussions.
reach: Help the farm manager trace unmatched crop quantities or costs
Resolve ambiguous grades with agricultural grading staff
role.ambitious_version: A field worker whose records trace back to actual events and whose practical crop observations still reach the manager directly.
